titles.en: The Masterpiece I Could Never Draw

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Raiden Lin plays the cheerful, slightly useless Lin son so well that the Syndicate and the police both ignore him. In fact he draws the family's safe rooms, and knows the weak point of every building in the city. One night he's kneeling in the middle of an illegal race on the old shipyard road, drawing a warehouse, and a motorbike stops two metres from him.

Jinx gets off it to beat some sense into him. He looks up, smiles, and tells her that her intake manifold is beautiful. The next morning he's at her garage near the Docks with three coffees. She drinks all three.

She grew up in a chop shop under the flyover and swore she'd never be owned by anyone again, least of all the Lins. He'd like to marry her. He asks on a napkin, drawn to scale. She says not yet. He keeps asking.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Raiden is the Lin who talks. In every other book he's in the background, cheerful, drawing something, being an idiot on purpose. I wanted to know what he was like when he stopped pretending, and who would be the first person he did it for. It had to be someone who'd see through him at a hundred and ninety kilometres an hour.

This is the lightest book in the series so far, and the most kissing. They get together in chapter three and never really stop. The trouble isn't whether they'll fall in love. It's her father's shop, his father's name, and two people who were each hidden as children learning to stop hiding each other.

He's rich, and he spoils her: a building, a dyno, a lathe, a hill. She's paying half. She insisted.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a warm, funny romance, but it has some hard moments:

• A man hit by a van, with injuries and a night in hospital (Raiden Gets Hit by a Car)

• A child hidden in a freezer for eleven hours, and a ten-year-old crossing a border alone (Memes at 2 A.M., Ten, Walking Home Alone)

• A threat against a loved one, a knife and an armed crew (Her Father Calls After Five Years, The Men Who Own Her Father, She Builds Her Way Out, Raiden Stops Playing Dumb)

• A remembered attempted assault on a teenage girl, which she fought off; not shown on the page (Her Father Says Sorry, She Lets Him In)

• A friend coming back injured, and grief and fear (The Masterpiece He Could Never Draw)

• A workshop fire and smoke inhalation (The Fire at the Shop)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
The black door — Jinx's first garage, near the Iron Docks, under an old sign that says TAI HING ROPE & CANVAS.
The shipyard road — Two kilometres of cracked concrete between the dead shipyard and the cranes. Illegal races at one in the morning.
Mrs. Tong's — The noodle place on the corner that only serves men off the container ships. The table by the fridge, back to the wall.
The Meridian — Raiden's glass tower in the Symmetrical Ward. Thirty-one floors. The desk man calls the pale green bike “the tram”.
The pale green bike — The one Jinx built him. Twenty kilometres an hour, lights like a train, a drawing board on the tank, a bell.
The steel room — Behind her tool wall. A light that comes on by itself, air, a line out, a warm lamp she added, and a tin of peaches.
The napkins — Thirty-one proposals, each drawn to scale, kept in his wallet where other people keep photographs.
Under the flyover — The Slums of the Industry, where the sun never gets in. Her father's shop, CAO MOTOR REPAIR.
The gap — Behind the scrap heap, between the wall and the pillar. On the archive drawings from 1974.
The triple — A 1973 two-stroke, three cylinders, a widowmaker. Seized for seven years. Ran at 5:40 a.m.
Oh-three-one-one — The day she left. The code to everything she owns.
JINX — The shop in the old chandler's warehouse three doors down, with a long low window anyone can see into. The sign she cut herself.
The stair — Behind the third shelf on the mezzanine. Two hours of fire board. Used once.
The driveway — One point two kilometres on the hill above the reservoir road. It is a racetrack.
The monkey — The passenger in a racing sidecar, who hangs off the side. Raiden says navigator.
Dyno — A rolling road that measures a bike's power at the back wheel.
Intake manifold — The pipes that carry air and fuel into the engine. Hers are all the same length, by hand.

chapters.title: Sketching in the Middle of a Race Track
chapters.desc: May 2021. An illegal race on the old shipyard road, a man kneeling on the tarmac drawing a warehouse, and a very angry mechanic who nearly kills him.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t hit him. Write that down. I want it on record that I didn’t hit him.” — Jinx

chapters.title: “Nice Intake Manifold” Is Not a Pick-Up Line
chapters.desc: He turns up at her garage the next morning with a sketchbook and three coffees. She drinks all three. It worked anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “I brought three because I didn’t know how you took it. Now I know. You take all three.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Socialite Everyone Ignores
chapters.desc: A gallery opening forty floors up. He plays the fool so well that the whole room believes him. She watches him count the exits and knows he isn’t one.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody shoots the boy who can’t find his own coat.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The First Kiss Smells Like Oil
chapters.desc: She throws the spanner. She misses on purpose. He has one rule, and he keeps it, and he pushes it as far as it will go, under a bike, on two creepers, in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “I said I’d go if you threw a spanner. I didn’t say what happens if you miss.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Raiden Gets Hit by a Car
chapters.desc: June 2021. It isn’t her fault. She stays at the hospital all night anyway. At dawn he asks her to go out the back before his family comes, and she goes.
chapters.epigraph: “I said go. I meant stay. I’ve never been so frightened of anything in my life as I was of them seeing you.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: A Bike That Goes Twenty Kilometres an Hour
chapters.desc: Three weeks of silence, one visit from Zhao Zhendong, and a pale green bike with a drawing board on the tank. Then the thirty-first floor, his rule, and a man in plaster who begs.
chapters.epigraph: “If you’re going to draw in roads, you do it on this.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Her Father’s Chop Shop
chapters.desc: August 2021. A roof across the road from a shop under the flyover, where she learned engines before letters. She doesn’t go in. He draws the window with her father in it.
chapters.epigraph: “I could strip a carburettor before I could write my name. My father thought that was a good thing. So did I, for a while.” — Jinx

chapters.title: He Asks Her to Marry Him on a Napkin Drawing
chapters.desc: September 2021. Mrs. Tong’s noodle shop, a paper napkin, a plan of their whole life drawn to scale. She says not yet. He says he’ll ask every month until she doesn’t.
chapters.epigraph: “One to fifty. The scale’s at the bottom. I wanted you to see I’d measured.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Trophy Husband Has Dinner Ready
chapters.desc: Autumn 2021. He moves into two rooms above a garage and cooks every night. She comes up the stairs to soup and a clean floor. Then flour, the kitchen counter, and an argument they don’t finish.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody has to cook. You’d put soup in a gearbox if I let you.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Roof That Will Never Fall
chapters.desc: Winter 2021 to spring 2022. A letter says her building has been sold. It has: to her. Then he shows her what the new walls are really made of, and what’s behind the tool wall, and the dyno.
chapters.epigraph: “Every wall in here is lying. Every one. They all look like plaster. I promise you none of them will ever fall on your head.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Meanest Engineer in the City
chapters.desc: April 2022. A charity gala, a column with terrible feng shui, and a racing driver with kitchen-scissor hair who finds his act very funny until he forgets to do it. Serafina Song becomes a client.
chapters.epigraph: “She could build a bike faster than you could crash it. I’d bet money. I’d bet your money.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Raiden Is Proud of Her for an Entire Week
chapters.desc: October 2022. Best in Show at the custom show in the north. He tells everyone. The doorman, the anchor woman, a bus. Everyone except his own family. Then he tells Zhao, and Zhao already knows.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d like everyone to know. I’d like a plane to write it in the sky. I’ve looked into it. It’s very expensive and the wind spoils the letters.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Memes at 2 A.M.
chapters.desc: December 2022. He can’t sleep, so he sends her memes from the next pillow. She knows why before he does. Then a farm in the borderland, a freezer, eleven hours, and a light that comes on by itself.
chapters.epigraph: “You built me a freezer with the light on.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Ten, Walking Home Alone
chapters.desc: January 2023. How a boy of ten copied a road map onto his arm, rode under the ice in a fish truck, and knocked on his father’s door. Then, at two in the morning, she goes to the Walled City for the first time, to see the door.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody was coming. So I went to them.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: A Commission From the Syndicate
chapters.desc: June 2023. Drawings on his table for a house on the Peak, and a room inside it that nobody can get into. She finally sees what he really does, and for whom, and what it could cost. They fight. They don’t finish the fight. Then he asks her to a wedding.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody looks at me. That’s the whole point.” “I looked.” — Raiden Lin and Jinx

chapters.title: Jinx Meets the Lin Family Properly
chapters.desc: September 2023. A flower shop, thirty people standing, a father in his funeral suit, and four sisters. “Jinx, my girlfriend, she built Xiao Pan’s bike, don’t touch her tools.” One very calm mechanic, and one very silent sister who nods.
chapters.epigraph: “You were the little girl under the bench. With the carburettor. I’ve always wondered what happened to you.” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: Her Father Calls After Five Years
chapters.desc: November 2023. A secret car built at night for a friend, a man who comes down at two in the morning and asks nothing. Then a phone call from under the flyover, a photograph of an old camp bed, and a note on the bench.
chapters.epigraph: “Gone to see my father. Don’t come. Back tomorrow.” — a note on the bench, in biro, on the back of an invoice

chapters.title: The Men Who Own Her Father
chapters.desc: Under the flyover, a polite man with reading glasses, a debt in stolen bikes, and a dead brother’s motorbike that hasn’t run in nine years. Then the useless Lin boy wanders in through the yard with a bag of dumplings, completely lost, with a floor plan in his jacket.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m terribly sorry. I think I’m lost. Is this the right flyover?” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: She Builds Her Way Out
chapters.desc: One night, one engine, three cylinders that haven’t moved in seven years. He holds the torch. Her father comes out of the office at three in the morning. At 5:40 the widowmaker coughs.
chapters.epigraph: “Two-strokes don’t forgive. They either run or they don’t. I like that about them. I like it about people too.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Raiden Stops Playing Dumb
chapters.desc: Quarter to six in the morning under the flyover. A deal broken, a knife, and the useless Lin boy steps in front of her and stops pretending. Then a black car at the end of the lane, and a brother-in-law who owes him one.
chapters.epigraph: “I know every building in this district. I know yours. You added two floors in 2019 on a frame drawn for four. Shall I tell you which beam?” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Her Father Says Sorry
chapters.desc: Winter 2023 to 2024. An old man at the black door for the first time, saying it badly. Then the red door, a Saturday dinner, a favour from Lin Jian that she refuses in his own kitchen, and fireworks over the Walled City at New Year.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody has said no to me in my own kitchen since 1987. Sit down. Eat. You’re family.” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: She Lets Him In
chapters.desc: March 2024. The thing that happened when she was seventeen, a steel box she’s had since she left, and the code to it. Then the thirty-first napkin, two creepers under a bike, to scale. Then a registry office on a Thursday, and a bike show in the north, in their good clothes.
chapters.epigraph: “Oh-three-one-one. The day I left. It’s the code to everything I own that’s mine.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Masterpiece He Could Never Draw
chapters.desc: May 2024. A friend comes back from the mountains with a hole in her husband. She pulls the roll-up door down and turns the radio up, and he sits on the pavement outside it. Then two in the morning, the bench, and for the first time in three years he gets her face.
chapters.epigraph: “I couldn’t draw you because you never let your face do anything. Tonight it did. That’s all it was. Three years.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Jinx Opens Her Own Shop
chapters.desc: November 2024. A fortune from a very large man for a house on a hill, an old chandler’s warehouse three doors down, his design, her name. A sign she cuts herself from steel. Then a customer in a good jacket who wants a bike nobody can catch.
chapters.epigraph: “His design. My name. My sign. I cut it myself. Nobody touches it.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Fire at the Shop
chapters.desc: June 2025. Two in the morning, a camera nobody asked for, and smoke coming out of the long low window. He runs three doors down barefoot. She comes out of the back lane through a stair he drew, black to the eyes. Then six weeks, and every Lin with tools.
chapters.epigraph: “I said the roof would never fall on your head. I didn’t say I’d be calm about it.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: “Is That a Racetrack?”
chapters.desc: October 2025. A drawing left on his desk on purpose: a house on a hill, a workshop on the roof under glass, two workbenches, and something long and curly in the garden. He says it’s a driveway. It is a racetrack.
chapters.epigraph: “Let me be rich at you. Just once. Just this. I’ve been practising for four years.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Roof Never Falls
chapters.desc: October 2026, a mountain hillclimb, sidecar class. She drives. He’s the passenger, hanging off the chair with pace notes he drew himself. They win by 1.4 seconds and kiss at the finish. Then the epilogue: a roof he designed, a spring night, and the lights across the lake.
chapters.epigraph: “I promised you the roof would never fall on your head. I didn’t promise I’d ever stop building you roofs.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Oil on His Cheek
chapters.desc: July 2022. He hovers. He shows her memes. He reads her the safety notices off the welder. She’s been under a gearbox for six hours. She started it.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve had my hands on engines all day. You’re the only thing in here I actually want to get my hands on.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Jinx Tries to Cook
chapters.desc: April 2023. The day after his birthday, which he always spends at the Walled City without her. She decides to cook him fish, the way he cooks it. The fire extinguisher is very efficient.
chapters.epigraph: “It was going very well until the oil.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Socialite Act at the Police Gala
chapters.desc: November 2024. A ballroom full of detectives, a husband who tells a superintendent his evidence room door is hung the wrong way round, and one very quiet inspector who isn’t fooled for a second.
chapters.epigraph: “He’s not stupid.” “No.” “I won’t tell.” — Inspector Song Wei Long and Jinx

chapters.title: Raiden Gets Lost in His Own Safe House
chapters.desc: February 2025. A house on the Peak, two cats called Topolino and Ritardo, a bookcase that shuts behind him, and the safest room in the city, which he designed far too well. He rings his wife from inside it.
chapters.epigraph: “I made it so nobody could open it from the outside. I’m very good. I’m the best in the city. I’d like to go home now.” — Raiden Lin, on the phone

chapters.title: The Golden Ratio Tattoo
chapters.desc: September 2025. Both her arms are full: peonies, gears, a carp. There’s one place left, on her right shoulder. She asks him to draw something for it. He draws it. She gets it. He nearly cries.
chapters.epigraph: “Every bit of me I chose myself. I wanted one bit you chose.” — Jinx

chapters.title: He Names Her Bikes
chapters.desc: 2026. She has never named a bike in her life. Bikes are bikes. He names all of them anyway, on little brass plates, without asking. She hates it. They all have names now.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s not a name. It’s a bike. Stop it.” — Jinx, to her husband, about Gerald

descs.en: He blew open a shipping container expecting guns and found a princess. She won’t go home. She keeps coming back.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lee Jun Hyuk goes to West Basin at two in the morning to kill the man who signs the papers. He blows the lock on the wrong container, expecting guns, and finds five women who have been in the dark for two days. One of them is standing in the middle of the box, between the door and the others, with her hands open.

He gets them out, leaves them at a hospital, and won't give his name. Evangeline Lin finds him anyway: a noodle menu on a dashboard, three days at a corner table, two bowls ordered every time. She is the Lin family's quiet daughter, the paper twin, and she has been somebody's secret since she was three days old. He is a big, kind, talkative man who hunts the people who move people, and he has a rule about everything.

She follows all of his rules except one. She keeps coming back.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Evangeline says almost nothing in Every Flower in the Shop. I always wanted to know what she'd say if somebody waited long enough, and the answer turned out to be: not much, and every word of it on purpose. So I gave her the man who talks more than anyone in the series. He talks to frightened people so they'll follow his voice. She's the first person who ever listened to all of it.

It's a dark book in places. He's done terrible things for what he thinks are good reasons, and the book doesn't pretend otherwise. But it's mostly about small things done in dangerous rooms: towels folded in thirds, a lamp left on, a window box behind bulletproof glass, a man practising a woman's name in the shower. And about what happens when the one person who never asks for anything finally asks.

He's rich, by the way. Very. He just never had anyone to spend it on. That changes in chapter fourteen, and then it really changes.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a dark romance with a lot of tenderness in it, but it has hard moments:

• Human trafficking: women held in a shipping container, and a lorry where eleven women died (The Container Had a Princess in It, Don't Stop Moving, She Asks Nothing, Someone Else Finishes It)

• Killings by the hero, mostly off the page (Don't Stop Moving, He Goes Hunting)

• An infected knife wound and a high fever, treated at home (The Night He Had a Fever)

• A dying man and morphine (The Target Is a Judge)

• A photograph of a captive sold online (The Traffickers Remember Her)

• A knife held to a father's throat, with no harm done (Jun Hyuk Meets His Father-in-Law (Badly))

• An abduction attempt, a head injury and a shooting (The Abduction Attempt, She Shoots First, After)

• A man found in a refrigerated container (Jun Hyuk Takes a Job He Hates)

• A sniper's choice on a riverbank (He Goes Anyway — Then Turns Back)

• A mother's death in an aid station, remembered by a child (The Borderland Boy)

• Grief for a parent the heroine never knew (A Letter From a Palace, The Throne Lets Her Go)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
West Basin — The container terminal where it starts. Row K, the old control tower.
Nam's Noodles — Eleven tables on River Bridge Road in the border town. Phones go in a jar between the chilli oil and the soy sauce.
The karaoke flat — Two rooms over a karaoke bar that closed in 2019. Painted windows, three locks, a camp bed.
The menu — Nam's takeaway menu, taped inside the door, with his rules on the back (and two of hers).
The textile building — Eight storeys by the harbour. He owns it. Sixth floor: five windows of glass you can shoot at all day.
The window box — A steel greenhouse bolted to a twenty-centimetre ledge, behind a hatch cut into bulletproof glass.
The rabbit book — His school exercise book of names, boats and payments. There are ten in the end.
The Grey Lanterns — The border unit that took him in at eight. Old Ko's unit.
The court language — The language of the country she was born in, which is never named. She taught herself.
The heron — The gold crest on her baby blanket: a heron over three peaks.
No. 9 Fig Tree Lane — The house with a real address. Thirty-one windows, and every one of them opens.
The Open Door — The foundation she starts for people who come out of boxes.
Rule seven — Don't come back.

chapters.title: The Container Had a Princess in It
chapters.desc: West Basin, two in the morning. He came to kill the man who signs the papers. He opens the wrong box.
chapters.epigraph: “If you want to live, stay behind me.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, row K, West Basin container terminal

chapters.title: Don’t Stop Moving
chapters.desc: The run through the stacks, a gap that hums, four minutes to wait, and the man he came to kill. She memorises everything.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back in four minutes, you’re in charge. You look like you’re already in charge.”

chapters.title: He Leaves Her at a Hospital
chapters.desc: Harbourside General, half past three in the morning. He won’t give his name. He doesn’t look back. She memorises his face anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “Name.” “No.” — the emergency entrance, Harbourside General

chapters.title: Evangeline Does Not Go Home
chapters.desc: Her father sends a car to the hospital. She sends it away. Then she asks Zhao Zhendong one question at five in the morning.
chapters.epigraph: “No.” — Evangeline Lin, to her father, for the first time in twenty-four years

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept Showing Up
chapters.desc: Three days at a corner table in a noodle shop by the river bridge, two bowls ordered every time. On the fourth day he sits down at the cold one.
chapters.epigraph: “She orders two bowls. Every time. One for her and one that goes cold. I’ve stopped charging her for the cold one.” — Old Nam, River Bridge Road

chapters.title: Lee Jun Hyuk Does Not Own Towels
chapters.desc: He dries himself with yesterday’s T-shirt. She notices. The next time she comes up the stairs, she is carrying three white towels. And on a Sunday, over a towel folded wrong, he asks.
chapters.epigraph: “You own something, you have to go back for it. Old Ko said that. Old Ko owned one spoon.”

chapters.title: Rules of a Safe House
chapters.desc: He comes home at three in the morning with someone else’s blood on his sleeve and finds the lamp on. So he writes seven rules on the back of a noodle menu. She follows six of them.
chapters.epigraph: “7. Don’t come back.” — the back of a menu from Nam’s Noodles, taped to the inside of a door

chapters.title: She Watches the Exits
chapters.desc: Footsteps on the stairs, the lamp off, and a back window he thought nobody knew about. She was there first. Then, in Nam’s back room, she tells him what she was raised to be.
chapters.epigraph: “Every house has a place where the sound carries. I’d found them all by the time I was seven.”

chapters.title: The Night He Had a Fever
chapters.desc: A knife wound he stitched himself, a week of lying about it, and forty degrees. For once in his life he can’t talk. So she does, all night.
chapters.epigraph: “When people are scared, you keep talking, so they hear a voice that isn’t scared, and they follow the voice.” — Sergeant Ko Baek-san, who never met her

chapters.title: Four Syllables
chapters.desc: Three weeks of healing, a spoon for his birthday, and a man who has gone quiet for the first time in his life. He’s been practising four syllables in the shower. She decides the rest.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s not a name. That’s a sentence.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, November, before he learned it

chapters.title: A Silver Ring With Coordinates Inside
chapters.desc: He’s going across the river for two weeks. The night before, cleaning the rifle at the table, he puts a plain silver band down beside her teacup instead of a proposal.
chapters.epigraph: “If I don’t come back, this ring has the coordinates to a life where no one can find you. If I do come back, you’re mine.”

chapters.title: The Target Is a Judge
chapters.desc: In 2016 a judge let the Ferryman walk out of court in a week. Seven years later Jun Hyuk climbs the stairs to his flat to finish it, and finds an old man waiting for him in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “I wondered when you’d come. I’ve been leaving the door unlocked since March.” — Judge Lo Wing-hang

chapters.title: She Asks Nothing
chapters.desc: In the dark, with her hand on his chest, he tells her about a truck on the river road in 2015. Two nights later the typhoon takes the power, and she lights the three candles from the drawer.
chapters.epigraph: “You opened mine.” — Evangeline, in the dark, on the twenty-second of June

chapters.title: Elowen Visits, Carrying Groceries
chapters.desc: Four bags of shopping, a dozen lemons from her mother’s tree, and the coolest look in the Walled City. Downstairs, an arms dealer waits in a car and a man who hates arms dealers goes down to talk to him.
chapters.epigraph: “I married a man who says one word. You found one who says all of them.” — Elowen Zhao

chapters.title: Evangeline Wants a Window Box
chapters.desc: A sixth-floor flat in an old textile building, a real stove, and windows made of glass you could shoot at all day. They don’t open. She mentions basil once.
chapters.epigraph: “Basil would grow here.” — Evangeline, not asking for anything

chapters.title: He Builds One Anyway
chapters.desc: A steel box bolted to a concrete ledge, a hatch cut into five layers of glass, and nine pots of herbs. Then a pair of earrings from Harbour Road, a flower-shop wedding, and a man on the roof across the street all night.
chapters.epigraph: “Good mend.” — Evangeline Lin, at a wedding, to Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: The Traffickers Remember Her
chapters.desc: There is exactly one photograph of Evangeline Lin in the world. It was taken with a flash in the dark of a container, and in October someone puts it up for sale.
chapters.epigraph: “Price on request. Serious buyers only. Palace interest welcome.” — a listing, deleted at 4:00 a.m.

chapters.title: He Goes Hunting
chapters.desc: A mahjong club above a car wash on Kiln Street, a man called Hwang, and four days. She follows every rule. She doesn’t sleep.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back by Sunday, go to your sister. Don’t wait up.” “I won’t.” — the sixth floor, Thursday night

chapters.title: She Washes His Hands
chapters.desc: Warm water, a nail brush, and ten fingers, one at a time. She doesn’t ask whose it is. In the morning he tells her the only part she needs: who answered the advertisement.
chapters.epigraph: “Why don’t you ask?” “Because you’d tell me.”

chapters.title: Jun Hyuk Meets His Father-in-Law (Badly)
chapters.desc: A tracker in a birthday phone, a lawyer’s letter in a locked drawer, and a knife held very still at the throat of the most frightening man the Walled City ever had. She is in the doorway when he says it.
chapters.epigraph: “She is no longer your asset. She is my wife. If you use her again, I’ll erase you.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, the fishing-net building, 18 November

chapters.title: A Letter From a Palace
chapters.desc: A man she never met has died in a country she has never seen, and left her something in his will. The letter is in two languages. She reads the one she was never taught first.
chapters.epigraph: “His late Majesty acknowledges a daughter, born on the seventh day of April 1998, and commends her to the care of his House.” — a letter, hand-delivered, 14 March 2024

chapters.title: The Envoy at the Door
chapters.desc: A polite man in grey gloves, a diplomatic passport, two guards on the step, and an offer with a husband already chosen. She asks him one question he won’t answer.
chapters.epigraph: “His Majesty would be pleased to receive you. Everything has been arranged.” — the Envoy, the Walled City, 6 April 2024

chapters.title: Evangeline Says No to a Country
chapters.desc: On her real birthday, in her mother’s front room, she answers the envoy in the language she taught herself in a library. Then he has the afternoon to arrange a birthday, and a great deal of money, and one new fact.
chapters.epigraph: “Tell His Majesty I am not a question to be settled.” — Evangeline, 7 April 2024, in the court language

chapters.title: Zhao and Jun Hyuk Share a Table
chapters.desc: Dinner for four at the house on the hill. Two sisters in the kitchen, two men on the terrace who would happily kill each other, and one sentence from Zhao Zhendong that changes the next month.
chapters.epigraph: “I sold rifles to the man whose boats took her. I didn’t know. I know now.” — Zhao Zhendong, on the terrace, 11 May 2024

chapters.title: The Abduction Attempt
chapters.desc: Old Nam’s seventy-fourth birthday, which she refuses to celebrate. A plan with Bao and two of Zhao’s men on the bridge. Then four men in a noodle shop at two in the afternoon, a pipe, and a choice she makes in about one second.
chapters.epigraph: “If you want to live, don’t stop moving.” — rule nought, which was never written on the menu because it didn’t need to be

chapters.title: She Shoots First
chapters.desc: Three shots in a noodle shop. The first two hit the duck cabinet. She is still very bad at it. It is enough.
chapters.epigraph: “Stay behind me.” — Evangeline, River Bridge Road, 15 June 2024

chapters.title: After
chapters.desc: Staples in his scalp, a scan he doesn’t want, a detective who knows exactly who he is, and a man with a diplomatic passport who finds out what it’s worth. That night she shakes for an hour. He holds her the whole time.
chapters.epigraph: “A diplomatic passport is a document. Immunity is a status. You have the first. You don’t have the second.” — Inspector Song Wei Long

chapters.title: Raiden and the Paper Twin
chapters.desc: Her brother comes to draw the man who can’t lift anything for six weeks, and tells her the one thing he’s never told anyone. Then Jun Hyuk hears the name of a farm on the river road, in the winter of 2007, and goes very quiet.
chapters.epigraph: “In the morning there was a tin of peaches on the gatepost. I never found out who left it.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Jun Hyuk Takes a Job He Hates
chapters.desc: He doesn’t need the money. He needs a name that holds, a payslip, and a life nobody comes through the door for. So he goes to work for the man he likes least in the city, opening every container at the Iron Docks with his own hands.
chapters.epigraph: “Every box that comes through my docks gets opened. By you. I don’t care what it costs.” — Zhao Zhendong, the Iron Docks, August 2024

chapters.title: The Throne Lets Her Go
chapters.desc: The twenty-first floor of the Harbour Hotel, a notary, a pen, and a man of forty-four with her face round the eyes. He signs her free. Then he gives her three things that were never in any folder.
chapters.epigraph: “Our father asked about you once a year, on your birthday. He asked if the problem was still moved.” — the King, suite 2101

chapters.title: A House With a Real Address
chapters.desc: No. 9, Fig Tree Lane. A front door, a garden that goes down to a stream, a glasshouse she didn’t know about, and windows that open. And a postbox with no name on it yet, because he’s waiting for her to choose.
chapters.epigraph: “Every window in this house opens. I checked them all. Twice.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, 12 October 2024

chapters.title: The Neighbours Bring a Cake
chapters.desc: Mrs. Bae from next door arrives with a chestnut sponge. He checks it for explosives. She eats a slice in front of him. Then a week of buying furniture with a man who never looks at a price, and a cedar chest her father carries up four stone steps on his own.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve lived on this lane fifty years. Nobody’s ever checked my cake before. I’m very flattered.” — Mrs. Bae, No. 7

chapters.title: He Doesn’t Know How to Sleep Without a Weapon
chapters.desc: Everything he used to keep under the bed is locked in a steel room behind the pantry now. So he lies awake facing a door he can’t see. She moves to his side of the bed, between him and the door, and stays there for a month.
chapters.epigraph: “You watch the door. I’ll watch you. That’s fair.” — Evangeline, No. 9 Fig Tree Lane, November 2024

chapters.title: The Last Target
chapters.desc: Old Nam rings on a Thursday night. The Ferryman is back on the river after nine years, with a boat and thirty people and a Saturday. Jun Hyuk goes into the pantry under the stairs, and she sits across the table every night and watches him clean the rifle.
chapters.epigraph: “He’s back. Gu. The grey suit and the toothpick. Saturday the seventh. The old jetty below the bridge.” — Old Nam, on the phone with the cord

chapters.title: Evangeline Asks Him Not to Go
chapters.desc: She has asked him questions, and asked him to teach her, and asked him to come here. She has never once asked him for anything for herself. On the Friday night before the boat, she does.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t go.” — Evangeline, 6 December 2024, the first thing she has ever asked for

chapters.title: He Goes Anyway — Then Turns Back
chapters.desc: The bank above the old jetty, eleven at night, a rifle, and a bag with ten exercise books in it. A boat comes across the river with thirty people on it. A man in a grey suit stands on the jetty counting money. At twelve forty-one, with the man in the scope, he rings her.
chapters.epigraph: “I can see him. I’ve got him. I can’t hear anything but you.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, the north bank, 12:41 a.m., 8 December 2024

chapters.title: Staying
chapters.desc: Ten exercise books handed through a car window at the bridge. A rifle carried down a bank for the last time and given away. Two and a half hours of road, and a woman standing at a green gate at four in the morning in her coat. The night he stays.
chapters.epigraph: “Put it in whatever room you put things in. I don’t want to know where.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, to Inspector Song Wei Long, 8 December 2024

chapters.title: Someone Else Finishes It
chapters.desc: Friday the thirteenth of December, six in the morning, a farmhouse on the far side of the river that is in the book with the frog on the cover. He watches it on a television in the inspection shed at the Iron Docks, on the bench, with her beside him and her lunch going cold.
chapters.epigraph: “Gu Shanlin, I’m arresting you.” — Inspector Song Wei Long, 6:04 a.m., 13 December 2024, on every channel by noon

chapters.title: A Wedding With Six Guests
chapters.desc: The longest night of the year, a garden in December, herbs from the glasshouse in her hands, six guests and a seventh in scrubs. She talks. He can’t. And her wedding present to him is something nobody has been able to give him since he was seven.
chapters.epigraph: “You said if you came back, I was yours. You came back.” — Evangeline Lee, 21 December 2024

chapters.title: Forgiven
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Three years later, the longest night of the year. Eleven rosemary bushes as high as the wall, a viola that sounds like a viola now, and a young woman in a nurse’s uniform at the gate with a letter.
chapters.epigraph: “I hold the hair now. Every shift. I wanted you to know.” — Nuo, at the gate of No. 9, 21 December 2027

chapters.title: A Princess at the Supermarket
chapters.desc: November 2022. She is twenty-four and has never once bought her own groceries. He follows her round the biggest supermarket in the border town at a distance of six metres, pretending not to, until the vegetable scales defeat her.
chapters.epigraph: “You have to weigh them first. Over there. And then it prints a sticker. Nobody tells you. I didn’t know for years either.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, aisle four

chapters.title: Lee Jun Hyuk Tries to Cook Breakfast
chapters.desc: November 2024, Fig Tree Lane. He wants to bring her breakfast in bed, once, like a husband in a film. The smoke alarm was not consulted.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve cleaned a rifle in the dark in four minutes. I can make an egg.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, 6:12 a.m., before the egg

chapters.title: The Neighbour’s Cat Chose Him
chapters.desc: Winter 2024. A ginger cat with half an ear, a terrible thief, decides that the biggest man on Fig Tree Lane belongs to him. The biggest man on Fig Tree Lane says he doesn’t like cats. Nobody believes him.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t like cats. I’ve never liked cats. Cats are a liability.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, with a cat asleep on his chest

chapters.title: Evangeline Learns to Shoot
chapters.desc: February 2024, a range in the hills that belongs to a man who owes him a favour. She asked him to teach her. She is very, very bad at it, and so serious about being bad at it that he can’t concentrate on anything else.
chapters.epigraph: “Again.” — Evangeline, after missing the target entirely for the fourteenth time

chapters.title: He Learns Her Favourite Colour
chapters.desc: October 2023, a year to the week after West Basin. He has bought her aquamarines and a pale blue coat and has never once asked. When he finally does, she doesn’t say blue.
chapters.epigraph: “Orange.” — Evangeline, the textile building, October 2023

chapters.title: The Borderland Boy
chapters.desc: Spring 1999. A boy of eight with a name written inside his collar, an aid station on a river road, and a sergeant with one spoon who decides, against every rule his unit has, to take him along.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s a big name for a small boy.” — Sergeant Ko Baek-san, reading a collar, 1999

chapters.title: Paper Twins
chapters.desc: April 2025. For seventeen years Raiden has said he’s the older twin, because he’s louder. Now there’s a king’s signature that says otherwise. He doesn’t accept it. So they have a party on the eighth, the day in between.
chapters.epigraph: “Paper beats silk. Everybody knows that.” — Raiden Lin, wrongly

chapters.title: He Talks for Both of Them
chapters.desc: The Chen Foundation Spring Gala, May 2025, as seen by Aurelia Chen. Elowen’s quiet sister has said eleven words to her in five years. Her husband has said several thousand to everyone else in the room, and has not let go of her hand once.
chapters.epigraph: “Your husband is the only man here who’s asked the waiter’s name.” — Aurelia Chen, to Evangeline Lee, who didn’t answer

chapters.title: The Silver Ring Engraving
chapters.desc: May 2026. Two lines of numbers inside a silver band, worn for three years and never once looked up. A boat that goes twice a week from a harbour nobody watches. A stone house with a fig tree, a wall behind a stove, and a way out that neither of them needs any more.
chapters.epigraph: “If I don’t come back, this ring has the coordinates to a life where no one can find you.” — the ring, April 2023. “Show me anyway.” — Evangeline, May 2026

chapters.title: Clean Towels
chapters.desc: October 2025. She goes to the lake country for four days with Mrs. Lai to play at the summer festival’s autumn concert, and he stays home with the cat and every towel in the house. When she comes back up the lane, they are all folded her way. Except one.
chapters.epigraph: “She does it in two seconds. It took me until four in the morning.” — Lee Jun Hyuk

descs.en: She saw through the guard nobody else noticed. He has spent ten years making people disappear, and now he wants to disappear with her.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
At a government reception on Battery Hill, sixty guards stand at the doors and look at the guests. One of them doesn’t. He watches a single man for forty-one minutes, and the only person in the building who notices is Serafina Song, there on a staff pass to inspect a red Lancia, in her sister’s dress and her own boots.

She walks across the ballroom and tells him he isn’t a guard. She’s right. Qin Haozhen has spent ten years making people disappear for a state that doesn’t put its name on doors, and nobody has ever looked at him before.

She finds his name with one bribed caterer. She asks him for a race, not a date. And a man who sleeps four hours a night in any bed in any country falls asleep in the passenger seat of her thirty-year-old car at three in the morning, and keeps coming back.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Serafina walked out of her engagement dinner between the soup and the fish in The Woman Who Sets the Price, and then turned up at her sister’s wedding in Milan with oil on her boots. I always wanted to know who could keep up with her.

The answer turned out to be the most forgettable man in the room. Haozhen is not a good man at the start of this book, and it doesn’t pretend he is. It’s about a man finding out he’s allowed to want something, starting with an egg sandwich, and a woman who decides every single morning whether she can live with the truth about him, and keeps deciding yes.

The racing is as real as I could make it: braking markers, tyre temperatures, driver changes, telemetry in four coloured lines. The spy work stays at the level of a story. And yes, the car really can do two hundred miles an hour. He did the brakes.

characters.title: Characters

chars.name: Serafina Song

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a fast, funny book, but it has some hard moments:

• A state operative’s work, including abductions and killings, mostly off the page and remembered (What He Does for Work, The Target Has a Family, Chen Si Brokers a Truce)

• A man taken from his family in front of his young son (The Target Has a Family)

• Trauma, depression and silence after a mission (He Comes Home Wrong)

• A cruel parent and a family’s financial collapse (The Song Family Opposes the Match)

• Threats against family members and surveillance (A File on the Workbench)

• A car chase, gunfire, a gunshot wound and a burning car (Shoot the Tyres), and a fever (The Safe House in the Mountains)

• Wound stitching without a doctor (The First Time He Bleeds in Her Garage)

• A serious racing crash, intensive care and a long recovery from concussion (The Needle, Hospital, Night Two, She Drives Again)

• Illegal street racing throughout Volume One

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Nonna — Serafina’s red 1992 Lancia Delta HF Integrale, named after their grandmother.
Gilded — Team AURELIA’s matte black race car, number 7, with AURELIA in gold on the bonnet.
Nobody — The getaway car: a grey 2006 Toyota Crown estate with wooden-bead seat covers and an engine it should never have had.
Two Hundred — A burnt-out 1991 endurance prototype, bought for scrap.
The garage — Under the railway bridge in the industrial district. Trains every eleven minutes.
Granny Shum’s — The Saturday street races by the paint works: the long straight, the S-bends, the lamp posts round the gas works.
The Needle — The hairpin at the end of the back straight at the circuit in the north.
The Eleventh — The Bureau Haozhen worked for, in a building with no name on it.
Brake on the marker — Braking exactly at the board, to the metre.
Telemetry — The car’s data: speed, throttle, brake and steering, a thousand times a second.

chapters.title: The Guard Nobody Else Noticed
chapters.desc: A government reception on Battery Hill, a car with a forged chassis plate, and the only guard in the building who never once looked at the guests.
chapters.epigraph: “Everyone in that room was looking at somebody. He was the only one looking at the right person.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Serafina Finds Out His Name
chapters.desc: It takes her three weeks, a leasing company that doesn’t exist, and one bribed caterer. Then he turns up under her shutter at two in the morning to ask her to stop. By ten past four she has done his brakes, and he has asked her to tell him to go.
chapters.epigraph: “A car tells you everything about the man who drives it. His just told me to mind my own business.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: A Race, Not a Date
chapters.desc: Granny Shum’s Saturday meet, four kilometres of factory road, and a grey estate car everyone laughs at. He accepts. He loses on purpose. She knows. Behind his car door, before the police come round the corner, he doesn’t lose anything else.
chapters.epigraph: “A circuit is a circuit and a road is a road, and I’m not giving up the road for anybody.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Rematch
chapters.desc: A track day at the circuit in the north, one red Lancia, two drivers and Mouse with a stopwatch. This time he drives like himself. She has never been happier.
chapters.epigraph: “He drove like someone signing his name. No flourishes. Every letter exactly where it belonged.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: 3 A.M., Passenger Seat
chapters.desc: He sleeps about four hours a night, in any bed, in any country. Then one night after Granny Shum’s, in the passenger seat of a thirty-year-old Lancia, he sleeps for two hours and eleven minutes.
chapters.epigraph: “In ten years I’ve never sat in a car I wasn’t driving or guarding.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: What He Does for Work
chapters.desc: A Belgian family reports a missing father. She lays the whole thing out on the workbench like a diagnosis, one part at a time, and waits for him to say she’s wrong. He doesn’t.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t lie to you. I’ve never lied to you. I just haven’t told you most of it.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: She Should Run
chapters.desc: Four days. Any sensible woman would run, and she knows exactly how. Instead she turns up outside his flat at six in the morning with two egg sandwiches from the place under the flyover.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to run. I’m the one people run with.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: The First Time He Bleeds in Her Garage
chapters.desc: Valentine’s night. He said eight o’clock, with dinner. He comes at ten to one with the dinner, cold, and a knife cut down his left forearm, because a Bureau doctor would write it down. She stitches him with fishing line and swears in three languages.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule two doesn’t cover blood. Sit down before you fall on my car.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Twelve Days and a Postcard
chapters.desc: “I’ll be gone. Maybe two weeks.” No calls. A pre-season test that nearly ends in the tyre wall at the Needle. A sister who notices everything. Then, on the twelfth day, a postcard with no words on it at all.
chapters.epigraph: “When you can tell me, tell me. That’s how it works in my house.” — Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: The Ring Was in the Glovebox
chapters.desc: She only wanted the tyre gauge. He had a plan in four parts and a speech he’d practised for eleven days. She says yes before he gets to part two. Then the coast road, the engine ticking, and the loft over the tracks, where they count trains.
chapters.epigraph: “I had a plan. It had four parts. You were supposed to let me finish.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Qin Haozhen Has Never Planned a Party
chapters.desc: He has stood at the door of eleven weddings and never once been inside one. Now he has a notebook, a run sheet for an engagement drinks timed to the minute, a form to fill in for the Bureau, and a fiancée who has just bought a burnt-out race car for scrap.
chapters.epigraph: “If I report it, she’s a fact. If I hide it, she’s a weakness.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Aurelia Finds Out Who Pays for the Racing Team
chapters.desc: A splitter that was already paid for. A gearbox from Germany nobody ordered on her account. A company with one director and ten years of salary behind it. Two sisters, one table at Da Gianni, and a lunch the whole restaurant will remember.
chapters.epigraph: “Your sister pays because she couldn’t go with you. I paid because I might not be able to stay.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Two Professionals at One Table
chapters.desc: The forty-fourth floor. Chen Si cooks. Aurelia gives back the ruby, resized with the last of their grandmother’s gold. And on the balcony after dinner, two men who are very good at the same things recognise each other without either of them saying what they are.
chapters.epigraph: “In my house we have a sentence for it. ‘I can’t tell you that yet.’ You’ll find it saves a great deal of furniture.” — Chen Si

chapters.title: Director Duan Sends Congratulations
chapters.desc: A tea house in the old town, a red scarf that has been on the needles since 2012, and a woman who never raises her voice. She has read his form. She knows about the braised beef. Her wedding present is a silver pen with a number engraved on it.
chapters.epigraph: “We look after our families, Haozhen. You know that. It’s in the training.” — Director Duan Qiuyan

chapters.title: Five A.M., Departures
chapters.desc: The last night before Lisbon, the loft, the trains. Then the airport road in the dark in a red Lancia, a brass tyre gauge he has to bring back, and three words through a car window that a traffic warden interrupts.
chapters.epigraph: “You have to bring it back. It’s the only one that reads true. I’ll need it for the hill climb.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Baizhang Pass
chapters.desc: Twelve point four kilometres, a hundred and fifty-six corners, a rock wall on one side and nothing on the other. She sets her tyres without the gauge. Seven time zones away, in a hotel lobby at four in the morning, a night porter and a man with a brass gauge in his pocket watch her climb.
chapters.epigraph: “A hill climb is a race against a mountain. The mountain doesn’t care. That’s what makes it fair.” — Big Wu

chapters.title: The Target Has a Family
chapters.desc: Lisbon. A yellow house with blue tiles, a man who waters geraniums, a woman who works nights at the hospital, and a boy of eleven who has been trying all summer to do thirty-two keepy-ups against the wall. The mission that cracks him.
chapters.epigraph: “Not in front of the house. Please. That’s my son’s window.” — Gong Ruiming

chapters.title: He Comes Home Wrong
chapters.desc: He comes in through the side door at four in the morning, gives her back the gauge, gets into the passenger seat of a car that isn’t going anywhere, and doesn’t speak for two days. She doesn’t make him. On the third night her sister rings about their father, and he finally tells her about a boy and a football.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to ask. I’m going to sit here. You talk when there’s something you can say.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: The Song Family Opposes the Match
chapters.desc: A letter in her mother’s handwriting. The house on the Peak, with numbered stickers on everything that can be sold. “A security guard?” Her mother asks him nine questions and he answers every one of them truthfully. They have no idea who he is. Then her mother says the cruellest thing she has ever said, and Serafina walks out of that house for the second time.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody keeps her, madam. I’d like to be wherever she is. That’s all I’m asking for.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Jinx Builds the Getaway Car
chapters.desc: “Sera, I want out.” Rule four, at last, at the kettle. But they know every car she owns. So it has to be a car nobody knows, built by a woman near the Docks with tattoos on both arms who builds bikes, hates cars, and takes one order at a time with no questions.
chapters.epigraph: “One order. No questions. And you never bring it back here with a hole in it.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Mission He Didn’t Take
chapters.desc: A grey building in the capital that isn’t on any map. A seventh-floor office with a radiator that knocks. A thin folder about a journalist in Singapore. For the first time in eleven years, he says one word to the state, and it’s the wrong one.
chapters.epigraph: “Do you know what happens to people who say no, Haozhen?” “Yes, Director. I’ve driven them.”

chapters.title: A File on the Workbench
chapters.desc: A Saturday afternoon. He’s in the north for his mother’s birthday. A woman of fifty-five in a grey coat ducks under the shutter with a shopping bag and her knitting, asks very politely for hot water, and sits on his stool. When she leaves, there’s a file on the bench. Forty photographs. One of them was taken that morning.
chapters.epigraph: “My mother did this with one photograph.” “My director thinks your mother’s an amateur.”

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.desc: Eleven years of black notebooks in his own code, hidden under a laundry cat’s heated bed. One line in a stolen ledger: two initials and the word “Private”. A month of nights at the workbench, Mouse at the end of it finding companies, and three copies of a file nobody in the capital knows exists.
chapters.epigraph: “Mr. Qin. For what it’s worth. You’re starting to exist.” — Qian

chapters.title: The Resignation Letter That Took Ten Years
chapters.desc: The New Year comes and goes and nobody calls. Lunar New Year comes and goes. So he goes to them, uninvited, on a Monday in February, with one sentence on a page torn from his notebook and the first page of an index. A quiet office, a radiator that knocks, and a woman who doesn’t stop knitting until she reads the word Northgate.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve spent ten years making people disappear, Sera. Don’t ask me to let go of the only person who ever made me feel visible.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: They Send Someone
chapters.desc: The season opener at the circuit in the north. Eleven thousand people in the grandstand, a black car with a gold name, and in the pit lane, with a hospitality lanyard and a stick of cinnamon gum, the boy from the next bed in a dormitory of forty, who once gave his window seat to nobody but him.
chapters.epigraph: “They always send the friend. It’s in the training. Better me than someone who doesn’t know you brake at the second lamp post.” — Mo Tianyi

chapters.title: Shoot the Tyres
chapters.desc: A closed service station on the old coast road, a car wash, and a grey taxi with the engine already running. Three cars behind them, then two, then one. She drives. He shoots out tyres. Nobody dies who didn’t have to, and one man who nearly does is pulled out of the fire by the friend he was sent to bring in.
chapters.epigraph: “You never bring it back here with a hole in it.” “We’ll bring it back, Jinx. I can’t promise about the hole.”

chapters.title: The Safe House in the Mountains
chapters.desc: A stone house above the tea terraces at Yunwu, a dead man’s photograph on the shrine, two deaf neighbours who bring eggs and ask nothing, a stray dog that stops dead in front of you, and rain on a tin roof. A fever, and then fourteen days with nowhere to be. The best two weeks of their lives.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody’s looking for us. For the first time in my life, nobody knows where I am.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Chen Si Brokers a Truce
chapters.desc: A black car in the tea terraces. A minister who has tea with Aurelia on the first Thursday of every month. A month of waiting, and then a quiet room in the old town where everything he ever wrote down goes into a stove. Two prices. He pays them both without asking. That night, at last, she asks him for the number, and he tells her.
chapters.epigraph: “There’s a price.” “Yes.” “You don’t want to know what it is?” “No.”

chapters.title: Disavowed
chapters.desc: Nine quiet months: a championship, a prize in Geneva, a man learning to sleep six hours and cook. Then a registered letter from the capital informs him that no person called Qin Haozhen has ever existed, and asks him to sign to confirm he received it. For the first time in years, he laughs until he can’t stand up. And with it comes a parcel, two metres long, in red wool.
chapters.epigraph: “They want me to sign to say I’ve received a letter telling me I don’t exist.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: A Man With No File
chapters.desc: A mining town that the maps stopped bothering with, a registry clerk who remembers a boy on the wall by the winding gear, and his mother at her Japanese sewing machine, who has never once believed he was a security guard. Then a driving test he fails for checking his mirrors too often. And Harbour Road, on a Friday afternoon, holding her hand where anyone can see.
chapters.epigraph: “Security guards don’t send that much money home, Haozhen. I’m not stupid. I’m a seamstress.” — Liang Shufen

chapters.title: The Song Family Was Not Invited
chapters.desc: Now that he exists, Mr. Kwok says, there has to be a proper engagement dinner. Six dishes, trestle tables, borrowed chairs, two mothers who have never met, and the trains every eleven minutes. Her parents were not invited. At eight o’clock, they come in under the shutter anyway, and her mother is carrying a folder.
chapters.epigraph: “I wasn’t invited.” “No, Mamma.” “I came anyway. I’m told that’s what people do in this family.”

chapters.title: Last Race in the Industrial District
chapters.desc: A works team from Modena wants her for the rest of the season and all of next. Page nine of the contract says she gives up the road. So she goes back to Granny Shum’s for one last Saturday, against a kid in a purple Nissan who was filming from a car roof the night she met the taxi, and a woman from Modena is standing in the crowd.
chapters.epigraph: “Rich girl. You’ll crash by Christmas.” “It’s been nine Christmases, Granny.” “Then you were lucky nine times. Stop now.”

chapters.title: Overqualified
chapters.desc: Orsini Corse needs a head of security for its Asian operation. His CV is one line long and says “References: none available.” Donatella Ferri asks why she should hire him. He tells her eleven things wrong with her paddock that he noticed on the walk from the car park. Then the twelfth.
chapters.epigraph: “Your CV is blank, Mr. Qin.” “Yes.” “Why should I hire you?” “Because I noticed eleven things on the way in.”

chapters.title: Pit Wall
chapters.desc: Speed traces, brake pressure, throttle, steering angle: four coloured lines on a screen, a thousand times a second. He learns to read them the way he used to read rooms. He finds something in her data nobody else has seen. And at the end of the pit wall, after three years, Mouse finally says a word to him.
chapters.epigraph: “Every driver lies to their engineer. The data doesn’t.” — Kenji Arakawa

chapters.title: The Needle
chapters.desc: The home round. Her parents in the grandstand for the first time. Lap thirty-one, the end of the back straight, a backmarker’s engine letting go a few seconds before she arrives. He sees it in the data before anyone sees it on the screens: brake pressure at maximum, and the speed not coming down.
chapters.epigraph: “The brake line is perfect. The speed isn’t falling. Kenji. The speed isn’t falling.”

chapters.title: Hospital, Night Two
chapters.desc: The ninth floor of the big hospital on the hill. A collarbone, three ribs, a bruised lung, a brain that has been shaken very hard. A machine breathing for her. “Family only,” says the nurse. Her mother says something nobody expected. Thirty hours later, at two in the morning, she opens her eyes and asks about the car.
chapters.epigraph: “He’s family. He’s more family than I am. Let him in.”  — Vittoria Song

chapters.title: She Drives Again
chapters.desc: Four months. A plate in her collarbone, headaches that come like weather, a red arm sling with a mountain road on it, and a simulator where she freezes at the Needle every time. Then a January morning at the circuit in the north. He doesn’t stop her. He holds her helmet.
chapters.epigraph: “What if my foot’s frightened?” “Then I’ll tell you. I’ll be on the wall. I’ll read it.”

chapters.title: Just Married, Two Hundred Miles an Hour
chapters.desc: A registry office at ten, where he finally gets a piece of paper that says what he is to her. Nine dishes in a garage under a railway bridge, and the middle of a wedding, at last, from the inside. Then rice, and a grey taxi, and the old military airstrip at dawn, where something red is waiting under a tarpaulin with his handwriting on its nose.
chapters.epigraph: “Two hundred miles an hour.” “You said it in miles.” “It sounds better in miles. Everything fast does. Someone told me.”

chapters.title: First Podium
chapters.desc: A whole season without one. Fourth, fifth, fourth, sixth. Then the finale at the circuit in the north, a year and a month after the Needle, with two mothers in Block C and a Ferrari in her mirrors on the last lap. Third place. Champagne in his face. He lets it happen.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t move.” “Sera.” “Don’t you dare move. Stand there. Look at me.”

chapters.title: A Garage With Two Names on the Door
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Two years on. The garage under the railway bridge has a sign at last. There’s a team, and a junior driver who used to film from a car roof, and three postcards on the whiteboard. One of them has a football drawn on it, and a number. And at three in the morning, someone different is driving the loop.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s got a sign now. Two names. Nobody’s ever going to walk past it again.” — Big Wu

chapters.title: Haozhen Learns to Lose at Karaoke
chapters.desc: December 2023: the team Christmas, in a karaoke room above Mr. Kwok’s favourite bar. Big Wu scores forty-one, Mr. Kwok sings for his late wife, and a man who has spent eleven years being forgettable tries hard to sing badly. She catches him lifting at the gas works.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re lifting.” “I’m not.” “You’re singing flat on purpose. I can hear it. Sing like yourself.”

chapters.title: Serafina Teaches Him to Change a Tyre
chapters.desc: December 2022, the week after the track day. She decides that any man who sits in her passenger seat should be able to change a wheel. He says he’s never done it. She times him: fourteen minutes. Then, one wet night in the alley, she sees him do it in ninety seconds.
chapters.epigraph: “You lied to me.” “I said I’d never done it in your garage. I’d never done it in your garage.”

chapters.title: The Security Guard Who Smiled Once
chapters.desc: August 2025, the Orsini paddock, as told by Callum Hart. There is a pool. Forty-one people have put money on who can make the head of security smile first. Callum tries jokes, a video of a goat, and an Italian mechanic in a wig. Witnesses are still recovering.
chapters.epigraph: “Has the security guy ever smiled?” “Once. On his pass photo. And we don’t know who at.” — the Orsini team group chat

chapters.title: Who Is Faster: Serafina or Jinx’s Bike?
chapters.desc: August 2024. An argument at Lunar New Year that has been going on for seven months. A track day, the main straight at the circuit in the north, a matte black car and a motorbike Jinx built from nothing. Everybody has a bet. Raiden is holding the money, which is the first mistake.
chapters.epigraph: “Off the line, it’s the bike. Over a kilometre, it’s the car. Over a whole lap, it’s whoever’s angrier.” — Big Wu

chapters.title: He Checks the Perimeter Before Breakfast
chapters.desc: Spring 2027. Every morning, before the egg sandwiches, he walks the garage: shutter, side door, alley, loft window, the roof hatch, the stairs. Every morning. She starts timing it. Four minutes and twelve seconds on day one. She keeps a chart on the whiteboard for a month. Then one morning he forgets.
chapters.epigraph: “I used to think all I wanted was a long life with you, where I didn’t have to check the perimeter before I kissed you.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: The Military Academy at Sixteen
chapters.desc: September 2010. A slow train south from a mining town, a dormitory of forty boys under a roof that leaks onto bed eleven, a firing range in the snow, and a boy who laughs with his whole face and gives away the window seat. Two years later, a woman with red wool on her needles asks a question about a map. The boy they chose because he never hesitated.
chapters.epigraph: “They told me he never hesitated. I asked him a question about a map. He answered it before I’d finished asking.” — Director Duan Qiuyan

chapters.title: Forty-Three Songs for the Car
chapters.desc: Nonna’s tape deck has been broken since 2017 and Serafina plays everything off her phone, in the same order, every time: forty-three songs, and she always skips the seventeenth. He doesn’t own a single piece of music. Over a summer he learns all forty-three, by heart, in order. Then he fixes the tape deck.
chapters.epigraph: “Why do you always skip seventeen?” “Because it’s my mother’s.” “Then why is it on there?” “Because it’s my mother’s.”

chapters.title: Wedding Planning With a Spreadsheet
chapters.desc: February 2026. Two hundred guests, nine round tables, one garage, and a laptop open on the long table on the forty-fourth floor. He has colour-coded everyone. There is a column for who must face the door. There is a column called “Score-neutral”. Aurelia reads it for an hour without speaking, and then says the nicest thing she has ever said to anyone who wasn’t her husband.
chapters.epigraph: “Column K.” “What’s column K?” “Whether they need to sit facing a door.”

chapters.title: Eliana Hacks the Bodyguard
chapters.desc: March 2025. Zhao is in Rotterdam and the youngest Lin sister is giving a talk about a bank that would rather she didn’t. Elowen asks for a favour. He has no identity card, no job and a brand-new phone. She has his phone open in four minutes. He is very impressed. She is very annoyed that he is impressed.
chapters.epigraph: “Four minutes.” “Three minutes and fifty seconds. I was being polite.”

chapters.title: The Fake Name He Liked Best
chapters.desc: May 2027, a ferry on Lake Como, on the way to see an old man with eleven cars and a parrot and a red Lancia with a forged chassis plate. He has had nineteen names. On the ferry, he tells her about the one he liked best: a deckhand called Ah Sang, on an island boat in a southern sea, whom nobody ever wanted anything from. She calls him by it once.
chapters.epigraph: “Ah Sang.” “No.” “No?” “Say the other one. I like the other one better now.”

descs.en: She proposed with eleven pages of terms. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

titles.en: The Woman Who Sets the Price

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
On the night of her father’s birthday, in front of two hundred guests, Aurelia Song’s mother raises a glass and announces that her daughter’s jewellery boutique is losing four million a year and will close in January. Aurelia walks out onto the balcony in gold silk, shaking, doing sums in her head. A stranger at the far end gives her his coat.

Six weeks later, the stranger walks into her boutique and asks to rent it. His name is Chen Si. He runs the Syndicate. He wants her shop for his business. She sets a price instead: a seat at his table.

Then she proposes. Eleven pages, in red ink, with terms. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

Between them stand a mother who loves only winners, a vice-minister who framed his father, a poisoned glass of wine on New Year’s Eve, a traitor at the table, and a woman who has never once in her life been loved without having to win.

The Woman Who Sets the Price is a sharp, glamorous, power-couple romance about a queen who refuses to be a title, and a man who never once asks her to win.

The main story is told across four volumes and is complete. Side stories at the end can be read any time. Aurelia and Chen Si first appear in Every Flower in the Shop and Proof by Induction, but this book stands on its own.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This book has some dark moments:

• A parent who humiliates her daughter in public, and emotional coercion within a family

• Organised crime, with threats and violence mostly off the page, and a car attack (A Snake in the Syndicate)

• A poisoning, intensive care and a long recovery (Volume Three)

• A panic attack and its aftermath, and therapy (The Word Is Milan)

• Memories of a parent’s wrongful arrest and death in custody, and of a riot and a stabbing in a juvenile detention centre (The Sewer, Nineteen Years Ago)

• Consensual power-play love scenes between a married couple, with a contract, orders, blindfolds, silk ties and a safe word. They are sensual but not explicit

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Aurelia Song was the rival in Every Flower in the Shop: gold, sunglasses, a slap in the rain, a running score. I wanted to know who she was at two in the morning, when nobody was watching her walk. This is her book.

The crime is kept at the level of a story; nothing here is a how-to. The jewellery is as real as I could make it: piercing saws, gravers, box links soldered one at a time, rouge on the wheel for the last pass.

Thank you for reading. Second is just the first of the ones who kept going.
