glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
AURELIA — Aurelia’s jewellery boutique on Harbour Road.
The Syndicate — The organisation Chen Si runs. Thirty years old, and older than him.
The terms — Aurelia’s price for laundering money through her shop: a share, real pieces, the books, no lies, a seat at the table.
The marriage agreement — Eleven clauses, renewable after ten years, when the Wife may rewrite every one. At the renewal, he adds a twelfth and a thirteenth.
Clause twelve — The Wife is not the Husband’s queen.
The word — The safe word written into the agreement. It is “Milan.”
Numero Uno — The necklace she named at two in the morning, after a phone call with her mother.
The Jade Hall — A restaurant on Temple Street with a round table for twelve. It has belonged to the Syndicate for thirty years.
The house on the Peak — Her parents’ house, where the party for her father’s fifty-seventh birthday was held.
The Song Group — Her father’s company.
The Pearl — The restaurant booked for New Year’s Eve, same as always.
Tesoro — Her father’s name for her, from before Vienna.

chapters.title: The Balcony Where He Lent Her His Coat
chapters.desc: Her father’s birthday. Her mother’s toast. The worst night of her life, and a stranger who didn’t try to fix it.
chapters.epigraph: “The world is obsessed with your shine. I’m more interested in what you do in the dark.”

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Rent Her Shop
chapters.desc: He came to use her boutique. He offered a very generous fee. She sent him back a counter-offer in red ink.
chapters.epigraph: “You want my shop. I want a seat at your table. Those are the terms.”

chapters.title: Aurelia Negotiates a Don Into a Corner
chapters.desc: She chooses a basement in the old town with eleven tables and no menu. He brings the books. She finds the hole in them before the second course. Under a streetlamp afterwards, he asks if he may kiss her.
chapters.epigraph: “You said I’d see the books.” “I said you would see them. I didn’t say I’d enjoy watching you read them.”

chapters.title: Aurelia Song Does Not Do Second Place
chapters.desc: Thursday. Five men who run the routes, one long table, and a woman they have been told to frighten. She sits in his chair, and kisses him in it. Then a game of mahjong she has no intention of losing.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule one of a room full of men who want you gone: sit down first.”

chapters.title: The First Ledger She Ever Read
chapters.desc: The Milan route, the first shipment under her name, a customs shed at the docks at four in the morning, and the realisation that she is very, very good at this.
chapters.epigraph: “It isn’t that I like breaking rules. I like knowing exactly which ones I’m breaking, and what they cost.”

chapters.title: He Never Asks Her to Win
chapters.desc: She tests him. She loses a game of chess on purpose. He doesn’t care. Then she finds out what he does care about, and it is not what she expected at all.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t care if you win. I care that you stop being afraid of what happens if you don’t.”

chapters.title: Dinner on the Forty-Fourth Floor
chapters.desc: He cooks. He tells her what happened to his parents, all of it. Then she gives him an order, and finds out how slowly a man can obey one.
chapters.epigraph: “Kneel.” He looked at her for a long moment. Then he did, without hurrying, as if he had been waiting for someone to ask.

chapters.title: A Proposal With Terms and Conditions
chapters.desc: Eleven pages, in red ink, on his own cream paper. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word. He reads every page, and signs every page, and then asks for an amendment.
chapters.epigraph: “Clause 9. In private, the Wife sets the terms, unless and until she says otherwise. Clause 10. The word is ‘Milan’.”

chapters.title: The Song Parents Are Not Told
chapters.desc: A Thursday in May. A palazzo on the Naviglio Grande. Eleven guests, a dress she designed in a week, and a mother in a villa forty minutes away who finds out from a magazine.
chapters.epigraph: “Shouldn’t we tell your parents?” “We will. They read Italian Vogue.”

chapters.title: Blood Brothers at the Reception
chapters.desc: Zhao Zhendong gives a speech of nine words. Serafina gives a warning. And on the wedding night, in a suite above the canal, the bride finds a use for her veil.
chapters.epigraph: “He is my brother. You are his. So you are mine.” — the complete best man’s speech of Zhao Zhendong

chapters.title: A Necklace on the Hit List
chapters.desc: He has been staring at a list of names for an hour. She drapes a sapphire collar worth more than all of them across his shoulders. He makes her count the stones.
chapters.epigraph: “My King, everyone on that list is worth less than this necklace. Look at me instead.”

chapters.title: Chen Si Lost an Argument (Once)
chapters.desc: It is about bodyguards. It is the only argument he has ever lost. It ends with Zhao Zhendong teaching his brother’s wife to shoot, and then fixing the dishwasher.
chapters.epigraph: “Clause four, darling. Half your people. I counted.”

chapters.title: The Song Family Is Coming to Dinner
chapters.desc: Four months after the magazine, a letter arrives in her mother’s handwriting. They would like to be proud of her. Aurelia knows exactly what that will cost.
chapters.epigraph: “Your father and I would like to come to dinner. We would like to be proud of you.” — Vittoria Song, letter, 2 October

chapters.title: What Her Father Wants
chapters.desc: Lunch at the best Italian restaurant in the city. Her father lays it out: a bridge, a signature, a minister, and his son-in-law’s name on a letter. Chen Si listens to all of it. Aurelia orders the risotto.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s only a letter. A few lines. Your name at the bottom. It would mean so much.” — Song Weiren

chapters.title: Aurelia Says No to Her Mother
chapters.desc: The house on the Peak, the morning room, three Italian maids pretending to polish silver. She says it in Italian, so that everyone understands. Then she goes shopping for Fu Kang.
chapters.epigraph: “No, Mamma. Not for the bridge. Not for you. Not ever.” — in Italian, so the maids understood too

chapters.title: Her Mother’s Last Card
chapters.desc: Vittoria Song does not lose. She has one card left, and it has Serafina’s name on it: an illegal street race, a jilted fiancé’s family, and a photograph in a police file.
chapters.epigraph: “You have something I want, tesoro. And I have your sister.”

chapters.title: The Racing Team She Pretends Not to Fund
chapters.desc: Six weeks to make Team AURELIA real. A gold logo on a black bonnet. A watch from Geneva in a box on Fu Kang’s table. And a mechanic who thinks the designer is a joke, until she rebuilds the sponsorship deck in a night.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t pretend to fund it any more.” “No. Now I pretend I’m not terrified.”

chapters.title: Sisters at a Racetrack
chapters.desc: The final race of the season. A black car with a gold name on the bonnet. A grandstand in the cold. Aurelia, who gets sick in the back of taxis, watches her sister drive at two hundred kilometres an hour, and does not look away once.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t watch the car. Watch the gap. The car goes where the gap is.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: My Queen Is Not a Title
chapters.desc: Christmas at the Peak. Two hundred guests, her mother in black, the vice-minister by the fire. Chen Si says two words out loud in front of the people who matter. Then, upstairs, in the room she grew up in, he makes her watch.
chapters.epigraph: “My queen.” It wasn’t a title. It was a warning, addressed to everyone in the room at once.

chapters.title: A Snake in the Syndicate
chapters.desc: A car on the coast road at two in the morning, and a lorry that shouldn’t be there. Someone inside is selling his schedule. Aurelia knows who. Chen Si knows too, and invites him to dinner.
chapters.epigraph: “Keep your friends close.” “I keep my snakes closer. Then I know which way they’re facing.”

chapters.title: The Glass of Wine at the Harbour Dinner
chapters.desc: New Year’s Eve on a boat called the Pearl. She chooses the wine. She opens every bottle herself. At midnight he takes her glass, because he only drinks what he takes. Twenty minutes later, his hand starts to shake.
chapters.epigraph: “I only drink what I take.” He took her glass. It was the only rule he had ever had that could be used against him.

chapters.title: The Week He Couldn’t Get Out of Bed
chapters.desc: A private room on the ninth floor with no name on the door. A heart that won’t keep time. A rumour, by the second of January, that the Don is dying. And a woman in yesterday’s gold, running everything in his name.
chapters.epigraph: “Food poisoning. Oysters. He’s furious. He’s working from bed.” She said it forty times in three days. She said it so well that she nearly believed it herself.

chapters.title: Aurelia Signs His Name
chapters.desc: Forty documents in three days. One forged signature, perfect. A transfer Sun Wei tries to slip through at midnight. And Enzo, at three in the morning, teaching her the last stroke.
chapters.epigraph: “Your si is too round. He doesn’t round anything. Look—he cuts it. Like a stone.” — Maestro Enzo Bellini, 3 a.m., 4 January

chapters.title: The Board Meeting Without a Don
chapters.desc: A private room in the old town, twelve men, one empty chair at the head of the table. Sun Wei has prepared a speech about continuity. Aurelia walks in alone, in black, and sits down before he can give it.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule one of a room full of men who want you gone.” She didn’t say it out loud this time. She didn’t have to.

chapters.title: The Traitor at the Table
chapters.desc: She invites the senior men to dinner on the forty-fourth floor. Eleven guests, a soup that takes eight hours, and a list of three names in her head before anyone picks up a spoon.
chapters.epigraph: “The glasses came from a caterer. The caterer has a brother-in-law. The brother-in-law has a brother-in-law.” She liked chains. She had built a career on them.

chapters.title: What She Does to the Traitor
chapters.desc: No gun, no knife, no Zhao. Just contracts, deeds, a frozen account, a forty-page file and one suitcase. By breakfast, Sun Wei owns nothing but the clothes he is standing in.
chapters.epigraph: “When someone hurts her, he doesn’t get loud. He gets quiet.” It turned out she did too.

chapters.title: Zhao Guards the Door
chapters.desc: Fourteen nights on a plastic chair outside a room on the ninth floor. A man with a syringe. A woman who falls asleep on his shoulder at four in the morning. Zhao Zhendong has never had a sister. He finds out what it is like.
chapters.epigraph: “He is my brother. You are his. So you are mine.” He had said it at a wedding in Milan. He had not known, then, that he meant it.

chapters.title: A Laptop, a Gun, and a Very Tired Co-Ruler
chapters.desc: His first night home. He wakes at three in the morning and she is in the chair beside the bed, asleep sitting up, with a laptop on her knees and a gun on the table and his necklace at her throat. He finally understands what he married.
chapters.epigraph: He had thought he married a wife. He had married a co-ruler, who slept sitting up with a gun on the bedside table, so that he wouldn’t have to.

chapters.title: He Is Weak for Six Weeks
chapters.desc: No stairs, no work, no anger, no sex, and he hates every minute of it. She makes him eat. On the forty-second day, when Dr. Ma finally says yes, she reads clause nine very carefully and finds a way to make sure he doesn’t lift a finger.
chapters.epigraph: “Nothing strenuous,” said Dr. Ma. “Then you won’t move,” said Aurelia. “At all. I’ll do it.”

chapters.title: The Word Is Milan
chapters.desc: The danger is over. He is safe. She is fine. She is fine for nine days. On the tenth, in the middle of the boutique, holding a champagne flute for a client, her hands stop working. She says the word for the first time, and it isn’t in bed.
chapters.epigraph: “If either party says it, at any time, in any room, in any circumstances, everything stops.” — Clause 10. She had always thought it would be in the dark.

chapters.title: The Collection Called “Balcony”
chapters.desc: A year after the boat. Therapy on Tuesdays. A florist from the Walled City married to her brother-in-law. And a collection about the worst night of her life, which she models for exactly one person, piece by piece.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re making jewellery about the night your mother humiliated you.” “No. I’m making jewellery about the man who didn’t try to fix it.”

chapters.title: The Paris Show
chapters.desc: Six days before the presentation, a rival house shows a coat-collar necklace that is hers, line for line. Someone sold her sketches. Her atelier is in pieces. She has three nights. He is in the front row, and does not look at his phone.
chapters.epigraph: “They stole the drawings. They can’t steal the hands.” — Maestro Enzo Bellini, Paris, 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Song Parents Ask for Tickets
chapters.desc: After Paris, everyone wants to see the collection in Asia. A letter arrives in her mother’s handwriting asking for two seats. Aurelia sends them. In the back row. Then her father comes to the front anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “We would be very grateful for two tickets.” It was the first time in twenty-five years her mother had written the word grateful.

chapters.title: Chen Si Takes a Day Off
chapters.desc: For the first time in eleven years, he switches off his phone at midnight and does not switch it back on. Nobody in the Syndicate knows what to do. She has planned the day. It involves a chess board, a bucket of ice, and rules.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule one. You lose a piece, you lose something else.” “That’s not chess.” “It is today.”

chapters.title: The Necklace She Makes for Him
chapters.desc: It isn’t jewellery. It’s a tag. Plain gold, on a plain chain, with three lines engraved on it in her hand, for a man who has spent his whole life waiting to be taken down the stairs.
chapters.epigraph: “If anyone ever takes you anywhere, at six in the morning, in your pyjamas, they will find this on you. And they will know who to call.”

chapters.title: Her Father Falls
chapters.desc: Shenzhen. Leverage. Four towers nobody will buy. Permits that won’t come. In eight weeks the Song Group goes from the second-richest family in the city to a story in the newspapers. Her father calls her at two in the morning. Her mother does not.
chapters.epigraph: “Tesoro. I don’t know who else to call.” — Song Weiren, 2:14 a.m.

chapters.title: Six in the Morning
chapters.desc: A locked drawer her mother never opened in front of anyone. A folder in her own safe, under the Geneva pieces. Eleven bankers around one table. And a hall in the Western District at six o’clock, where two people stand side by side and watch a grey man go down the stairs.
chapters.epigraph: “When it is done, she will be standing in the hall beside him at six in the morning. And then they will go and have breakfast.” — Clause 5

chapters.title: Number One, By Her Own Rules
chapters.desc: 2024. A collection called “Seconda”, made from every second place she ever came. A prize in Geneva that nobody from Asia has ever won. Her parents in the front row, and a daughter who does not look for them once. And afterwards, in a hotel suite above the lake, a medal on a ribbon and a man who is not allowed to touch it.
chapters.epigraph: “The winner sets the terms.” “You always set the terms.” “Tonight I set them in first place.”

chapters.title: Renewing the Contract
chapters.desc: Ten years to the day. Clause eleven says she may rewrite every clause. She has been drafting for a year. He has been preparing for longer, and he has a counter-offer, and a pen, and a book that cost a back-room doctor three days of stitches.
chapters.epigraph: “11. This agreement will be renewed after ten years, on the anniversary of its signing, at which point the Wife reserves the right to rewrite every clause.”

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sets the Price
chapters.desc: Epilogue. October, and the house on the Peak, bought at auction by a woman who told nobody she was bidding. A party for her father’s seventieth on the same balcony, in a different coat, with the same man waiting at the end of it in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “Who are you?” “Someone who doesn’t like lobster.” — the balcony, October 2018. “Who are you?” “The woman who sets the price.” — the balcony, October 2031

chapters.title: Floral vs. Jewelry, Round Forty-One
chapters.desc: A charity lunch. One centrepiece budget. Two women who were first and second at school, and who have not stopped keeping score. Their husbands sit at the end of the table and say nothing, which is the most dangerous thing either of them can do.
chapters.epigraph: “Forty-one.” “Forty. You can’t count the time I slapped you.” “I absolutely can.”

chapters.title: Chen Si Has Never Been Late. Today He Was Late.
chapters.desc: He made the dinner reservation himself, for seven. By half past, his phone goes to voicemail, and so does Zhao’s. For forty minutes, Aurelia finds out how much of her is still sitting in a corridor outside an ICU.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re late.” “I know.” “You’re never late.” “I know. I’m sorry. I had to go and get something, and it fought back.”

chapters.title: What the Don’s Assistant Puts Up With
chapters.desc: Qian has worked for Chen Si for twelve years. He has two drawers of antacids, a spreadsheet titled “Clause Nine Scheduling Conflicts”, and a theory that the most dangerous man in the city is completely, catastrophically, embarrassingly in love. A week in his life.
chapters.epigraph: Qian’s calendar, Monday, 9:00 a.m.: “Mr. Chen – Rotterdam call.” Qian’s calendar, Monday, 9:01 a.m.: “Mr. Chen – Rotterdam call (cancelled; Mrs. Chen came in).”

chapters.title: Blood Brothers Go Anniversary Shopping
chapters.desc: Two of the most feared men in the city. One shopping centre. Three hours before closing. Both their anniversaries are on the same week, and neither of them has bought anything, and one of them has never been inside a shop that sells things that aren’t guns.
chapters.epigraph: “What does she like?” “Me.” “That’s not a gift, Zhendong.” “Hm.”

chapters.title: Aurelia Loses at Mahjong to Evangeline
chapters.desc: Aurelia Chen has not lost a game of mahjong since she was nineteen. Elowen’s quiet sister has not said more than eleven words to her in five years. One Lunar New Year, one table, four players, and a husband standing behind his wife’s chair who is enjoying this far too much.
chapters.epigraph: “Pung.” — Evangeline Lee, the only word she said for two hours

chapters.title: The Sewer, Nineteen Years Ago
chapters.desc: Chen Si has told this story once, to nobody, in his head, every night for nineteen years. Tonight his wife asks about the scar on his arm, and he tells it out loud. Block C. The riot. A boy who came down off the top bunk without deciding to. And half a kilometre of freezing water in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t leave them behind you. Not ever. Everything you leave behind you comes back.”

chapters.title: Aurelia’s Rules for Galas
chapters.desc: The Shen Foundation gala, December 2025, from the other side of the room. Eleven rules, written on cream paper in red ink and slipped into her husband’s pocket at six o’clock. He has annotated every one. In black. In the car.
chapters.epigraph: Rule 1. Arrive after Elowen. (Annotation, in black: “You have arrived after Elowen at every event for seven years. She has started arriving later on purpose. One day you will both arrive at midnight.”)

chapters.title: Chen Si Reads Her Reviews
chapters.desc: He has kept every review since 2018, in a folder on his laptop called “Rotterdam (Q3)” so nobody will ever open it. One night she finds out he doesn’t only read them. He answers them, under a name she would know anywhere.
chapters.epigraph: “Who is LiftedAtEveryTurn?” “I have no idea.” “Clause three.” “…Ah.”

chapters.title: Milan in August
chapters.desc: The city is empty. Everyone who matters has gone to the lakes. The palazzo where they were married is closed for the summer and she has the only key. There is a problem, though, and it is clause ten: the safe word is the name of the city they are standing in, and every waiter in Milan keeps saying it.
chapters.epigraph: “Clause ten. Temporary rider. While physically present in the city of Milan, the word is ‘Rotterdam’.” “Why Rotterdam?” “Because nothing about Rotterdam has ever been sexy.”

chapters.title: The Ring She Designed Herself
chapters.desc: For three weeks, her husband gets out of bed at two in the morning and comes back at five smelling of polish. Aurelia Chen does not do jealousy. Aurelia Chen follows him anyway, in silk pyjamas and a coat, with a gun in her bag, and finds him somewhere she never expected: at her own bench.
chapters.epigraph: Sketchbook, age fifteen, first page, in pencil: “A ring for someone who is loved without having to win. (Mamma says: sentimental. Second-rate. Don’t waste the paper.)”

descs.en: He has one rule: nothing happens while she’s his student. She has a calendar with 266 squares, and an end date.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Dr. Miles Wei, 31, lecturer in physics, holds office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Shen Yu Jie, final-year student and the best mind in the department, comes on Wednesdays. Every Wednesday. With problems she has already solved.

He has one rule: nothing happens while she is a student in his department. He draws it on his chalkboard as a flat line. She adds an end date. 20 June, 16:00. Then she makes a calendar, two hundred and sixty-six squares long, and draws a physically inaccurate atom in every one.

Between them stand sticky-note physics jokes, a department that has started a betting pool, a supervisor who smokes on a balcony she isn’t allowed on, a mother who calls her daughter the Perfect Jewel in front of guests, a diplomat with a secret, and a grant nobody applied for.

Proof by Induction is a bright, slow-burn campus romance about waiting, about being taken seriously, and about a man who stopped laughing at seventeen and a woman who makes him start again.

The main story is told across four volumes and is complete. Side stories at the end can be read any time. Miles first appears as a side character in Every Flower in the Shop, but this book stands on its own.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a gentle book, but it has some hard moments:

• Emotional control and coercion by a parent, including being cut off financially and made to leave home (Volume Two and Volume Three)

• Online gossip and sexist rumours about a student (Rumours in the Department Kitchen)

• A character coming out to his family at a dinner table, and a parent walking out (The Perfect Jewel Says No)

• Illness with a high fever (Miles Gets Sick and Nobody Notices)

• A relationship between a lecturer and a student that stays strictly non-romantic until she has graduated, and is declared to the department

• Love scenes between the couple after graduation. They are sensual but not explicit (Yu Jie Gets a Job, The Night She Made Him Dance in the Empty Lab)

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Miles Wei walked into Every Flower in the Shop for one scene, dropped his clicker, asked Elowen if she was happy, and wouldn’t leave my head. This is his book.

I wanted a love story where the most romantic thing anyone does is take the other person’s mind seriously, and where waiting is not a delay but the point. The physics is real, kept at the level of a story: the harmonic oscillator, entropy as counting, strained graphene, and analogue black holes made in water tanks, which real laboratories build.

The jokes are, regrettably, also real. Thank you for reading.

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Wednesday — The day Yu Jie comes to office hours, which are on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The harmonic oscillator — The problem she brings on her first Wednesday. Its lowest energy, ½ħω, is never zero: nothing is ever completely at rest.
Lecture Theatre C — Where Miles teaches second-year Quantum Mechanics at ten, to a hundred and forty students.
The rule — Miles’s one rule: not while she is a student in his department.
The sticky notes — His physics jokes on the side of her tea. She catalogues every one, with a type, a rating out of ten and an annotation.
White Rabbit — The milk sweets Yu Jie keeps in her cardigan pocket. She writes on the wrappers.
The Perfect Jewel — What her mother calls her in front of guests.
Shen Holdings — Her family’s company. It owns half the harbour and a forty-storey building downtown.
Bell Street — The street by the old wall where the bakery called Fang’s stands.
Old Huang — The security guard at the blue door, eleven years on the night shift.
The red envelope — Twenty yuan from Tao Tao’s grandmother. Yu Jie never spends it.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Definitely Not Stuck on Quantum Mechanics
chapters.desc: Shen Yu Jie walks into his office with a problem she solved last year. He solves it anyway. Badly, on purpose, she thinks. She’s wrong.
chapters.epigraph: “I have a question about the harmonic oscillator.” “It’s Wednesday.” “I know.”

chapters.title: Office Hours Are Tuesdays and Thursdays
chapters.desc: She comes on Wednesdays. Every Wednesday. He starts leaving the door open.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s not small enough. You made it up. You decided it was small because it was easier.” — Yu Jie, to Dr. Miles Wei, on the wrong day

chapters.title: The Harmonic Oscillator Is Not a Metaphor
chapters.desc: She makes it one anyway. He explains zero-point energy to a room full of second-years and accidentally confesses something.
chapters.epigraph: “Nothing is allowed to be completely at rest. Not even at absolute zero.” — Dr. Miles Wei, Quantum Mechanics, Lecture 7

chapters.title: Miles Wei Has One Rule
chapters.desc: He turns her down kindly, with a diagram on the chalkboard. He accidentally gives her a date.
chapters.epigraph: “Not while you’re a student in this department.” “And when I’m not?” “…I didn’t think about that part.”

chapters.title: A Countdown Disguised as a Semester
chapters.desc: Yu Jie makes a calendar. Miles finds it and says nothing. Then he sets her a problem whose answer is the number of days left, walks her to the back stairs, and breaks his own rule.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a very well-made calendar. The atoms are a good touch. Physically inaccurate, but a good touch.”

chapters.title: The Coffee Cup Physics Jokes Were Not Flirting
chapters.desc: They were absolutely flirting. It starts with a sticky note on a mug, then another, then a war, and Dr. Fang is keeping score.
chapters.epigraph: “Why can’t you trust atoms? They make up everything.” — sticky note, yellow, Wednesday

chapters.title: Her Supervisor Is Very Interested
chapters.desc: Eight a.m. with Professor Gao, on a balcony where smoking is forbidden. Then Gao climbs the stairs to the fourth floor.
chapters.epigraph: “A man like Wei will hold to a rule until it kills him. Make sure it isn’t you it kills.” — Professor Gao Meiling

chapters.title: A Study Group of One
chapters.desc: She drags him to the library café on a Saturday. Her friends are terrible at thermodynamics. He is terrible at leaving.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a study group. Physics is allowed.” “It’s a café.” “Physics happens in cafés. Ask Einstein.”

chapters.title: Miles Gets Sick and Nobody Notices
chapters.desc: Except one student, with soup, a thermometer, a lecture he ends with a kiss, and his sister on speakerphone.
chapters.epigraph: “This is not allowed.” “I’m a student delivering soup. It’s community service.”

chapters.title: He Laughs in a Seminar
chapters.desc: The first time in fourteen years. The whole room goes quiet. Then an invitation arrives with a family crest on it.
chapters.epigraph: “Dr. Wei laughed.” “Out loud?” “Out loud. Zhou dropped his pen.” — overheard, fourth-floor kitchen

chapters.title: Miles in a Rented Suit
chapters.desc: He looks like he’s about to defend a thesis. His sister takes over. Dr. Fang provides croissants and terrible advice.
chapters.epigraph: “Black tie means a bow tie, Miles. Not a black tie.” — Wei Lan, on video call, despairing

chapters.title: The Shen Family Gala
chapters.desc: The Perfect Jewel at the top of the stairs. Two married women who recognise him across the room. And a very large man by the pillar, glaring.
chapters.epigraph: “Miles Wei. As I live and breathe. In a tuxedo.” — Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: Yu Jie Is Not Jealous of Women Married to Dangerous Men
chapters.desc: She is a little jealous. She would like that noted privately. Then Aurelia Chen corners her in the powder room.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not jealous.” “You’ve folded that napkin into a swan, unfolded it, and folded it into a smaller swan.”

chapters.title: Elowen Asks Him One Question
chapters.desc: Five years ago he asked her on a balcony. Tonight, on a terrace over the harbour, she asks him back.
chapters.epigraph: “Are you happy, Miles?” He had never once, in thirty-one years, thought about it.

chapters.title: The Diplomat Her Mother Chose
chapters.desc: Lu Zhiyuan is a perfect match on paper: twenty-nine, five languages, a beautiful waltz. Yu Jie hates paper. Then he offers her a deal.
chapters.epigraph: “On paper, we’re perfect.” “I hate paper.” “Good. So do I. Shall we dance anyway?”

chapters.title: Miles Takes the Long Way Home
chapters.desc: One in the morning, no coat, silver shoes that hurt. He walks her home through the sleeping city, three metres apart under the streetlights and not at all along the old wall, and stops one block early on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re walking very slowly.” “I’m calculating the optimal route.” “It’s a straight line, Miles.” “Not if you do it properly.”

chapters.title: The Thesis Draft Covered in Red Pen
chapters.desc: He’s not her supervisor. He reads it anyway, all night, and finds the flaw that would have sunk her in May. She fixes it her way, and that night she crosses the snowy sports ground to his flat.
chapters.epigraph: “This is beautiful. Now prove it.” — margin note, page 41, red ink

chapters.title: Rumours in the Department Kitchen
chapters.desc: A photograph on the student forum. A man’s tuxedo jacket at half past one in the morning. Then Miles hears what the postdocs are saying, and finds out he has a temper after all.
chapters.epigraph: “The Shen girl’s buying her degree, and he’s getting paid in kind.” — Dr. Ren Bo, fourth-floor kitchen, Tuesday, 12:31 p.m.

chapters.title: Miles Recuses Himself
chapters.desc: One page, written at his one table between midnight and four. The most honest document in the history of the department. Then the Wednesday rules change, and Fang Hao brings croissants.
chapters.epigraph: “I have a personal interest in this student. I wish to state clearly what it is, so that nobody else has to guess.” — Dr. M. Wei, letter to the Head of Department

chapters.title: She Cries in a Stairwell
chapters.desc: New Year’s Eve dinner at the museum, with the Lus at the table and the forum on her mother’s phone. Not because of him. Because of her mother.
chapters.epigraph: “I let you have your little hobby. I let you have your little man. Now the hobby is over.” — Shen Ruolan

chapters.title: The Grant Nobody Applied For
chapters.desc: Five years of funding, a laboratory with a water tank that bends light, and a donor who wants no name. Miles is overjoyed for exactly two days.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody gives four million to a theorist, Miles. Nobody. Theorists are cheap. We need chalk and a chair.” — Dr. Fang Hao

chapters.title: He Finds the Name
chapters.desc: A purpose clause in a trust deed, signed with three initials. Then a diplomat in a perfect suit comes to Thursday office hours with no physics question at all.
chapters.epigraph: “To fund research into the bending of light, under the direction of a scientist who takes students’ questions seriously.” — Deed of the Bending Light Foundation, clause 2

chapters.title: Their First Real Fight
chapters.desc: An intercom by a blue door, in the rain. “You bought me a lab.” “I bought you time.” Both of them are right. That’s the problem.
chapters.epigraph: “You bought me a lab.” “I bought you time. There’s a difference. You’re a physicist. You of all people should know the difference.”

chapters.title: Two Weeks of Not Speaking
chapters.desc: Wednesdays are empty. He keeps the door open anyway. Fang Hao eats for two. Somewhere in the basement, a water tank is waiting.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s 5:30. She’s not coming.” “I know.” “Then why are you still sitting here?” “Because she might.”

chapters.title: Yu Jie Gives the Money Back
chapters.desc: The fortieth floor of the Shen Building, alone, with four pens in her hair. Her father has never once asked her about an equation. Today, he asks.
chapters.epigraph: “Your grandmother said you would come here one day and ask me for something. She said I should listen.” — Shen Guoqiang

chapters.title: The Perfect Jewel Says No
chapters.desc: Sunday dinner at the museum, with the Lus, a seating plan for two hundred, and a sample of engagement silk. She puts down her chopsticks. Then the diplomat puts down his.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not a jewel, Mother. I’m a physicist. You can’t wear me.”

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.desc: The bank card fails at the canteen. A letter from the family office. Seven days to leave. She packs one suitcase, and finds out what she owns.
chapters.epigraph: “Insufficient funds.” — card reader, City University canteen, Monday, 12:41 p.m.

chapters.title: Miles Finds Her a Room
chapters.desc: Not his. A slanted attic above a bakery on Bell Street, a landlady who once threw a rolling pin at a health inspector, and bread at four in the morning. He carries the suitcase and doesn’t go in. On the night of his review, she asks him up.
chapters.epigraph: “Rent is two hundred a month and four mornings a week on the counter. Fair is fair. Nobody in my house lives on charity.” — Su Mei, baker

chapters.title: The Thesis Defence
chapters.desc: Nearly three hours in room 301, with an external examiner from the capital who has a score to settle. Miles waits in the corridor and doesn’t sit down.
chapters.epigraph: “Miss Shen. Tell me about your boundary conditions.” — Professor Zhou Lin, 10:47 a.m.

chapters.title: Graduation Day, 4:01 P.M.
chapters.desc: The ceremony ends at four. Eighty-seven steps from the Great Hall to the fourth floor. A door left open on purpose, and the first kiss anyone else has ever seen.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s open. Unless you’re from facilities.” “I’m not from facilities.” “No. I know.”

chapters.title: A Proof by Induction
chapters.desc: Sunday, a closed building, a key. Miles asks her out the only way he knows how: on a chalkboard, with a base case, an inductive step, and a very small mistake he made on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “Let P(n) be the statement: on day n, I want to see you on day n + 1.”

chapters.title: The First Date Has a Lesson Plan
chapters.desc: Four pages, timed to the minute, with learning objectives. She reads it, folds it into a paper plane, and takes him to the night market instead.
chapters.epigraph: “Learning objective 3: by the end of the evening, the participant will feel comfortable.” “Miles, I’m going to throw this into the harbour.”

chapters.title: Holding Hands in Public
chapters.desc: Across the campus in July, past the canteen, the library café and the department kitchen. He keeps checking whether anyone is looking. Everyone is. Then a society photographer gets the picture the forum never did.
chapters.epigraph: “Dr. Wei. You can stop looking over your shoulder. You’re allowed.” “I know I’m allowed. My shoulders don’t.”

chapters.title: Yu Jie Gets a Job
chapters.desc: A research assistant post in the capital, five hours north. He asks her what she wants, and makes himself listen to the answer. Then the last night of August, the door of the staff flat, and a question he asks at every step.
chapters.epigraph: “What do you want?” “I want both.” “Then we’ll find out how to have both. I’m a physicist. I’m good at problems with two variables.”

chapters.title: Long Distance Is Just a Variable
chapters.desc: The 18:20 and the 21:10. Calls at midnight. A whiteboard screwed to his kitchen wall. A storm, a cancelled train, a handsome postdoc, and a black hole made of water that finally holds.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d like to report that I’m jealous. I don’t think it’s rational. I’m reporting it anyway, in the interests of transparency.”

chapters.title: Her Mother Comes to Tea
chapters.desc: No warning, no appointment, pale grey silk on a basement ramp. Mrs. Shen inspects the physics lecturer, his tank, and his only clean mug. He explains entropy. She brings something she was supposed to have thrown away.
chapters.epigraph: “Messy is more likely than tidy, Mrs. Shen. There are more ways to be messy.” “And you think that’s a good thing.” “I think it’s a true one.”

chapters.title: Miles Meets His Own Past
chapters.desc: A flower shop in the Walled City on a Saturday in May. Elowen and Aurelia, together, at last on the same side, telling him he finally chose correctly. And a glass globe that has been quietly setting the roses on fire.
chapters.epigraph: “We fought over you in a library for a week.” “Eight days.” “He counted. Of course he counted.”

chapters.title: The Apartment With Two Desks
chapters.desc: A one-line letter to the Head of Department. Two flights up on Bell Street. Two second-hand desks that face each other, and a cactus that moves house in a bicycle basket.
chapters.epigraph: “I have a personal interest in Dr.-to-be Shen. I have no academic authority over her. I would like this noted. I would also like it noted that I am very happy.”

chapters.title: A Ring Hidden in a Problem Set
chapters.desc: The second Wednesday of September, two years on, 3:47 p.m. Three problems on graph paper, a man who is a very bad liar, and a 113th sticky note.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve got a problem I don’t know the answer to.” “You’re lying.” “How can you tell?” “Your ears.”

chapters.title: Quod Erat Demonstrandum
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Two red booklets in the morning. A garden behind the Hall of Science at 4:01 in the afternoon. A blackboard on an easel, a cake covered in Bohr atoms, and a proof that is finally finished.
chapters.epigraph: “Q.E.D. Which was to be demonstrated.”

chapters.title: Who Hid Miles Wei’s Glasses (Again)
chapters.desc: A short investigation, conducted by Dr. Fang Hao, into the fourteenth disappearance of a pair of glasses on Bell Street. There is one obvious suspect. There is also a motive nobody expected.
chapters.epigraph: “Case file 14. The glasses were last seen on the subject’s face. The subject cannot see the case file.”

chapters.title: The Night She Made Him Dance in the Empty Lab
chapters.desc: Midnight in the basement of the east wing. One pair of headphones, two people, a horizon holding in a tank of water, and a man who has never danced in his life.
chapters.epigraph: “I can’t dance.” “You can walk the long way for forty-one minutes. Dancing is just the long way, in a circle.”

chapters.title: Miles Calculates Before Holding Hands
chapters.desc: The second date. A cinema, a shared armrest, and a man with a napkin and a pencil in the dark, working out the optimal moment. She has already done the calculation. Hers is shorter.
chapters.epigraph: “Let θ be the angle of the armrest. Let t be the time elapsed since the lights went down. Let me be an idiot.”

chapters.title: The Sticky Note Archive
chapters.desc: For his thirty-fourth birthday, she gives him a binder. A hundred and twelve sticky notes, catalogued, dated, cross-referenced, and annotated. Some of them he doesn’t remember writing. One of them she never showed him.
chapters.epigraph: “Note 47. Yellow. 28 Jan. ‘Why can’t you trust an atom? They make up everything.’ (Second use. He forgot he’d already done it on 29 Oct. I didn’t tell him.)”

chapters.title: Zhao Zhendong Is Glaring at Me From Across the Room
chapters.desc: The Shen Foundation gala, from inside Miles’s head. A running log of one arms dealer’s stare, the reunion he has spent five years being embarrassed about, and the moment the glaring changed direction.
chapters.epigraph: “19:42. Still glaring. I have moved four metres to the left. The glare has moved four metres to the left.”

chapters.title: Miles Tries to Text With Emojis
chapters.desc: The long-distance year, as told through a phone. The atom is not romantic. The cactus is a cry for help. And one message, at 2:14 in the morning, that needed no emoji at all.
chapters.epigraph: “Miles. Why did you just send me a picture of a test tube.” “It’s an emoji. Ouyang says people use them to express feelings.” “What feeling is a test tube.” “…Excitement?”

chapters.title: Yu Jie Teaches First Years
chapters.desc: Doctoral student, first-year problem class, Thursday mornings, room 104. She is terrifying. They are terrified. By November, there is a queue outside the door on the wrong day.
chapters.epigraph: “There is no such thing as a stupid question in this room. There are only questions you haven’t asked yet, and those are the stupid ones.”

chapters.title: The Department Christmas Party
chapters.desc: The first department party Miles Wei has attended in seven years. There is a quiz. He wins it. There is also karaoke, a dumpling race, a secret gift exchange and a dance-off with the Head of Department. She wins everything else.
chapters.epigraph: “Round Six: Physics. Dr. Wei, would you please stop answering before I’ve finished the question.”

chapters.title: Physics Puns, Ranked
chapters.desc: A speech at their first anniversary dinner, in the back room of a dumpling stall at a night market, by the woman who has heard all his jokes. Fifteen of them, ranked, with notes.
chapters.epigraph: “I have been asked to say a few words. I have chosen, instead, to rank his jokes. He has agreed to this. He says it is a fair test.”

chapters.title: Miles at Sixteen
chapters.desc: The year before the library. A boy at the back of the advanced physics class who does impressions of the teacher, a tired girl at the end of his table, a girl who reads his notebook out loud, and eight days that taught him to stop wanting things. And the man who, fourteen years later, unlearned it.
chapters.epigraph: “No girlfriends until university.” — Wei Miles, aged sixteen, front page of a physics notebook

descs.en: She married the arms dealer to protect her father. He has never stopped wondering whether she married him for love.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lin Elowen is a florist in the Walled City. Her father moves cargo for Zhao Zhendong, the arms dealer the whole city is afraid of. When three of Zhao’s containers are seized and her father is blamed, Elowen walks into Zhao’s office at the Iron Docks and does something nobody expects.

She asks him to marry her.

It is a contract, three pages long, in her neat handwriting. Separate rooms. Her own shop. You don’t touch me unless I ask. He signs it without arguing. He knows exactly why she wants him, and it isn’t love.

Every Flower in the Shop is a slow-burn romance inside a marriage: a woman who married a dangerous man to protect her family, and a man who would burn the world down for her and still can’t bring himself to ask the one question that matters. Did she ever choose him at all?

The main story is told in order across four volumes and is complete. Side stories at the end can be read any time.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a dark romance. The love story is tender, but the world around it is not. The book includes:

• The illegal arms trade throughout, including weapons sold to militias that use child soldiers (A Shipment With Children’s Names on It)

• Torture and on-page killing by the hero: broken fingers, a stabbing through the hand, a man burned on purpose, near-drowning, shootings, and a killing in a garden pond (Volume One; Forty-Eight Hours)

• Unwanted touching at a dinner table (The First Dinner as Mrs. Zhao)

• Arson and serious burns (The Night the Delivery Van Burned)

• A drive-by shooting at the shop, with a child present, and a neck wound (Glass, Nobody Else Touches Her)

• A gunshot wound, infection and surgery on a kitchen table without anaesthetic (He Crawled the Last Mile)

• Child abuse in a character’s past, described briefly (Thorns at Six in the Morning, Fifteen Years Ago, Block C)

• A violent prison riot and stabbing (Fifteen Years Ago, Block C)

• Family betrayal, and grief for a mother who died in childbirth

• Love scenes between the married couple. They are sensual but not explicit (Page Two, Line Six, The Estate in the Rain, The Flower in His Lapel and others)

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
After The Softest Kind of Love, I wanted to write the other kind: a love that is quiet because it is so big, between two people who are not soft at all.

Zhao Zhendong is not a good man, and this book won’t pretend he is. Elowen knows exactly what he does. What she doesn’t know, for a long time, is what to do with the fact that the most frightening man in the city sits outside her bedroom door every night so she won’t have to wonder where he is.

The flower shop details are real: the 4 a.m. market, cutting stems with a knife at an angle, the cooler kept just above freezing. The arms trade is kept at the level of a story. Thank you for reading.
